transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
I just don’t care about my painting or the garden anymore, and the things I used to look forward to feel like a burden. It just feels like too much effort to do anything these days.
Have you ever had a similar period of feeling depressed or losing interest in things before, or is this the first time?
I don't recall ever feeling quite like this before this year. Usually, I've been able to keep up with my gardening and daily life without any trouble, so this heavy feeling is very new to me.
Over the past two weeks, have you also had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration?

Yes, I've been struggling with almost all of that lately. I feel bone-tired no matter how much I lie down, and I have to force myself to eat because food just feels like a chore. My mind also goes completely blank or spins when I try to make simple decisions, like trying to schedule our appointments.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. I'm just feeling incredibly tired, empty, and overwhelmed by everything right now, but I don't want to die.
How long have you been feeling this way continuously, and has it been most of the day nearly every day?

This heavy, tired feeling has been with me continuously for about three months now, ever since I crashed after that busy spell in the spring. It is there pretty much all day, every single day, and I just can't seem to shake it.
Have these symptoms been present nearly every day for at least two weeks without a break, or do they come and go?
Yes, it has been completely constant without any break at all. For the last three months, ever since I crashed after that busy spell in the spring, I've felt this heavy and tired every single day.
Have you ever had a period of at least a few days where you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did things that were out of character for you?

Yes, back in the spring I had a spell where I felt strangely revved up, overly cheerful, and quite touchy at times, which is not like me at all. I was talking a mile a minute, jumping from one idea to another, and barely sleeping because my mind was racing with plans to revamp the community center. It was a complete contrast to how I normally am, and I felt like I had endless energy.
How long did that revved-up period in the spring last, and did it cause any problems at work, with relationships, or lead to risky behavior?

That revved-up period lasted for several weeks—about a month—before I completely crashed. It did cause problems; I was snapping at my daughter when she tried to slow me down, and I completely neglected my own doctor visits. I also overcommitted so much at the community center that I had to step back, and I even started mixing up my husband's appointments and prescriptions.

During that revved-up period in the spring, did you ever need to be hospitalized, or did you do anything very risky or clearly out of character, like spending a lot of money, driving recklessly, or having impulsive sexual behavior?

No, I wasn't hospitalized, and I didn't do anything extreme like reckless driving, spending sprees, or impulsive behaviors. However, my family definitely found my constant racing around and over-committing at the community center to be very out of character for me.
During that revved-up period in the spring, did your symptoms make it hard to function at work, at home, or in your relationships, even if you were not hospitalized?

Yes, it did cause significant problems for me. I had to step back from most of my community center work, and I started missing or mixing up several of my husband's appointments and prescriptions. It got to the point where my daughter had to start coming over almost daily to help with things I've always managed on my own.
During that revved-up period in the spring, did the symptoms last at least 4 days in a row, or did they continue for a week or more?
Oh, it lasted much longer than just a few days or a week. That revved-up period went on continuously for several weeks—about a month, actually—before I finally crashed into this low feeling.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a clear past hypomanic/manic-spectrum episode lasting about one month with elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, racing thoughts, increased goal-directed activity, and marked functional impairment, followed by a current 3-month depressive episode with anhedonia, fatigue, appetite change, and poor concentration. This longitudinal pattern is most consistent with bipolar disorder (ICD-10 F31).
